pseudocode:
adfu_check(arg):                                   ; 0xb4069254, arg = ini word +0x14 (1 in every release)
  reg  = halfword[0xb406b9d4]                      ; 0x35
  s    = pmic_read(reg) & 0xffff                   ; I2C error -> -1 -> 0xffff
  printf("pmu_status = 0x%x\n", s)
  if s & 2:                                         ; only bit 1
      pmic_write(reg, s & ~3)                       ; result ignored
      goto enter                                    ; GPIO untouched
  if arg == 0: return
  if word[0xb4064c00] == 0: return                  ; boot code 0 (SD0) returns here
  PULLCTL1 = PULLCTL1 & ~(1 << 17)                  ; not restored
  in_saved  = CINEN ; out_saved = COUTEN
  COUTEN &= ~(1<<10) ; CINEN |= 1<<10               ; C10 input
  CINEN  &= ~(1<<11) ; COUTEN |= 1<<11              ; C11 output
  shift = 0x55aa55aa ; rx = 0
  for i in 0..31:                                   ; no early exit
      CDAT = CDAT & ~(1<<11)                        ; write 1
      CDAT = CDAT | ((shift & 1) << 11)             ; write 2 (fresh read, no clear)
      shift >>= 1
      delay_ms(1)
      rx |= ((CDAT >> 10) & 1) << i
  CINEN = in_saved ; COUTEN = out_saved
  if rx != 0x55aa55aa: return
enter:
  printf("Prepare to entry ADFU mode\n")
  tail-call rom_reentry_adfu()                      ; 0xb40691a4

register_allocation.r4: status & 2, then loop counter i (0 on the test path)
register_allocation.r6: status register number, then drive shift register

dependencies: timer 0 running (delay_ms -> delay_us polls 0xb0168010, set up by timer_init)
PMIC/I2C bus selected by pmu_init (pmic_read re-selects bus [0xb4070864])

pmic_rules.always_read: Register 0x35 is read and printed on every call, before the argument and boot-code guards.
pmic_rules.write_back: status & ~3 written back (bits 0 and 1 cleared, bits 15:2 kept) through pmic_write; its return value is ignored; then ADFU. The GPIO registers are not touched on this path.
pmic_rules.precedence: PMIC bit 1 > argument == 0 > boot code == 0 > loopback result.
pmic_rules.read_failure: pmic_read returns -1 on an I2C error with no retry (0xb4069610); & 0xffff gives 0xffff, bit 1 is set, so a failed read of reg 0x35 enters ADFU and writes back 0xfffc.
pmic_rules.i2c_bound: The I2C transfer (0xb406a994) polls at most 501 x delay_ms(1) before failing (not exercised here: the transaction layer is a register file).
pmic_rules.register_meaning: Not established. The loader prints it as "pmu_status" and treats bit 1 as an ADFU request. No pinned ATC2603C source or document was available offline to name reg 0x35; no write-one-to-clear or other semantics are assumed. The register file only stores the write.

gpio_registers.name: GPIO_COUTEN
gpio_registers.bits: 10 cleared, 11 set during the test; restored
gpio_registers.semantics: output enable per bit (name; behaviour not verified)

gpio_registers.name: GPIO_CINEN
gpio_registers.bits: 10 set, 11 cleared during the test; restored

gpio_registers.name: GPIO_CDAT
gpio_registers.semantics: Whether a read returns the output latch, the pad level or a mix is NOT established; the model offers "mixed" and "latch". Every write is a read-modify-write of the whole word, so under "mixed" the latch bits of other input pins (and C10) are rewritten with their sampled levels.

gpio_registers.name: PAD_PULLCTL1
gpio_registers.semantics: Vendor ATM7059 pinctrl data: bit 17 is the P_SD0_D0 (= GPIOC10) pull field, value 1 = pull-up, no pull-down; so clearing it most likely removes the pull-up from the sampled input. Electrical effect not verified.

sources.meaning: PAD_PULLCTL1 bit 17 = P_SD0_D0 pull, width 1, pull-up value 1, no pull-down value
PAD_PULLCTL1 bit 16 = P_SD0_D1 pull (not touched by the test)
values 0 SD0, 1 NOR, 2 reserved, 3 JTAG, 4 UART2, 5 UART5
SD0 data/cmd/clk groups muxed to sd0
D0/D1 groups as UART5 (serial5_default and mmc_share_uart)

board_mfp_init_sd0_fields.order: board_mfp_init runs before adfu_check, so these values are in place during the loopback test
board_mfp_init_sd0_fields.note: Field-to-function mapping from the vendor ATM7059 pinctrl data used by the RG35XX vendor kernel; not verified on silicon.

interpretation.claim: GPIO C10/C11 are the SD0 DAT0/DAT1 pads (P_SD0_D0/P_SD0_D1).
interpretation.confidence: strongly-supported for the pad identity; ball and connector wiring not seen

interpretation.claim: SD0 is the TF2 slot on the original RG35XX.
interpretation.basis: PR #8 (BOOT-023, STOR-003; DT sd_card on b0230000)

interpretation.claim: The loopback therefore tests DAT1 -> DAT0 of the TF2 card slot while the unit boots from SD2.
No shipped DTB uses pins 74/75 as plain GPIOs (buttons, card detect, power); they appear only as SD0 data (mmc0_default) and as the optional UART5 pair (serial5_default, mmc_share_uart).
board_mfp_init (ini+0x0d = 1) muxes SD0_D0, D2, D3, CMD and CLK to the vendor JTAG function before the test; D1 is left as the Boot ROM/reset left it.

Purpose: a factory/service fixture in the TF2 slot that connects DAT1 to DAT0 (and drives no pull) would make an SD2-booting unit enter ADFU. This fits the evidence but is a hypothesis; no Actions document, fixture description or board schematic was available.

Contradictory or alternative readings: the vendor DTS comment lists the same pads for UART2/UART5 debug use; a UART adapter in TF2 is another plausible intended partner. Whether GPIO enables override the JTAG mux on this pad is unknown.

assumptions: strict mode: any access in 0xb01b0000..0xb01b0100 outside the modelled registers is reported as unexpected (answers 0); pass-through mode (strict=False) stores such writes and returns them, logging each access, for whole-path runs where other routines legitimately use the block.
Register addresses and names from the vendor header regs_map-atm7039.h (pinned); semantics not verified.
OUTEN/INEN/PULLCTL reads return the last value written.
DAT read semantics are a selectable hypothesis (mixed: OUTEN -> latch, else INEN -> pad input, else undriven constant; latch: always the latch).
Pad input levels are synthetic rules of the model clock and of other pins' latches; pull, mux, electrical drive and propagation delay are not modelled.
Pin mux is not modelled: GPIO enables are assumed to control the pad whatever MFP_CTL selects.
Sample windows are delimited by gaps of window_gap_us between DAT accesses on the model clock, which the harness advances (synthetic timer reads or requested delays).

harness_rules.timer: T0 count word (timer base+8, 0xb0168010): +24 per read (1 synthetic us per read)
harness_rules.pmic: PMIC I2C transactions (0xb406ac10 read / 0xb406ac60 write) served by a register file (Pmic)
harness_rules.pre-state: I2C bus 1 pre-selected (0xb4070864 = 1, 0xb406ba10 = 1) as pmu_init leaves it

stalled_timer.outcome: instruction budget exhausted (emulator bound, not a firmware timeout)
stalled_timer.note: delay_us 0xb40693f8 polls with no iteration bound; the firmware implements no timeout. The run ends only because the emulator stops at its instruction budget.

registers.temporary: 64 writes: per iteration bit 11 cleared, then set to the pattern bit; every write is a whole-word read-modify-write
registers.final: bit 11 = last pattern bit = 0. Under "latch" read semantics every other bit is unchanged. Under "mixed" read semantics the latch bit of every non-output pin is rewritten with the level read: bit 10 = the C10 level at the second read of the last iteration (just after bit 11 was cleared), other input pins = their input level, pins with neither enable = the undriven value (scenarios init-mixed-*, init-unrelated-bits-undriven-high)
registers.conditional: bit 11 changes only if it was 1; the rest depends on the unknown read semantics and on the initial direction registers

persistent_state.mux: The test does not write any MFP register.
